newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower on lackluster cash markets.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower on lackluster cash markets.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended slightly lower Monday in response to lackluster cash markets, CBOT floor sources said.
"Cash is just dead, and these (CBOT) prices are too high," said one floor trader.
Trade was extremely light, with volume estimated at only 200 contracts.
That figure compared with Friday's actual volume of 486 contracts.
"This is the slowest day we've had since last summer," said a veteran pit trader.
Quiet export markets also weighed on futures, traders said. Thai rice is currently trading around $330.00 per tonne, but further weakness is expected.
"They (Thailand) are going to keep lowering prices until they find some business," said a trader.
Additionally, Costa Rica on Monday canceled a tender for 30,000 tonnes of rice, citing high prices.
Rice closed one to eight cents per cwt lower with May down eight at $11.40.
